title: Do Bigger Images Look Better? Two Models Compared from 0.1 to 1.0 Megapixels
summary: One prompt, 10 resolution tiers on each of two text-to-image models: both peak at 0.6MP; Z-Image Turbo never takes more than 4.1s at any tier, Flux 2 Klein 9B tops out at 18.3s

stats: 10 images per model, changing only the resolution (256×352 → 896×1120); the prompt, seed (91720260, the number that controls generation randomness) and sampling settings all stayed fixed
Z-Image ▮ 2-4.1s, barely moves — high resolution costs no extra wait; Flux2 ▮▮▮▮▮ 4.6→18.3s, rising linearly with pixels — 2-4x slower for the same image

Style comes from the model, not the resolution: all ten Z-Image tiers lean photoreal (low res only blurs, never shifts style), all ten Flux2 tiers stay locked in cel-shaded anime (a flat-color animation look)
Both models are best overall at 0.6MP (672×896): Z-Image 4.1s, Flux2 10.4s — matching the conclusion of the H3 video sweep
No: from 0.9→1.0MP neither model's file size grows, and one even shrinks — more time spent, but no extra information in the image
findings: No tier anxiety with Z-Image Turbo: all ten tiers finish in under 4.1s, so just keep 0.8MP as your daily default
Flux2 Klein's quality floor sits at 0.4MP: below it, limbs and linework break down, and rerolling over and over won't save them
Style comes from the model, not the resolution: same seed (the number that controls generation randomness), same prompt, and the two models already look completely different from 0.1MP up
Use Flux2 for anime subjects, Z-Image for real-person/cos (cosplay photo look) subjects — the latter is also 2-4x faster
